title: Max Chunks To Make Sorted
summary: Given an integer array representing a permutation of [0, n-1], determine the maximum number of chunks that can be split and sorted individually to form a sorted array when concatenated.
statement: Given an integer array representing a permutation of [0, n-1], determine the maximum number of chunks that can be split and sorted individually to form a sorted array when concatenated.
constraints: Partition into contiguous chunks, sort each independently, and concatenate.
Return the maximum chunks that produce globally sorted order.
hints: A chunk may end at i exactly when the prefix contains values 0..i.
For a permutation, that holds when the prefix maximum equals i.
Scan with a running maximum and count equality positions.
Every valid boundary is independent, so cutting at all of them maximizes the number of chunks.
editorial: Every valid boundary is independent, so cutting at all of them maximizes the number of chunks.

tests.explanation: No proper prefix contains exactly its target values, so only one chunk works.
The first two values form one chunk and each later value can stand alone, totaling four.
